scope: Deployment-dependency availability research only. This is not Norns inference, latency, RSS or acceptance evidence.
question: Does an official prebuilt ONNX Runtime for linux armv7l (32-bit armhf) CPython 3.9 exist for the Norns target?
verdict: NO official prebuilt ONNX Runtime artifact for linux armv7l has ever been published, for any version or any Python version.

primary_evidence.pypi_enumeration_method: https://pypi.org/pypi/onnxruntime/json enumerated over all releases; independently reproduced by the primary agent, not accepted from delegation alone
primary_evidence.github_releases: microsoft/onnxruntime Linux ARM assets are exclusively onnxruntime-linux-aarch64-<ver>.tgz; no armhf/armv7/arm32 asset in any release
primary_evidence.official_build_doc_statement: https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/build/inferencing.html states the recommended ARM path is ARM64 only (no support for ARM32)

secondary_blocker.statement: Independent of architecture, the last onnxruntime release publishing cp39 Linux wheels is 1.19.2; 1.20.0+ ships no cp39, and 1.24.1+ requires Python >= 3.11.

build_from_source_assessment.arm32_still_build_supported: cmake/linux_arm32_crosscompile_toolchain.cmake remains on main; ARM32v7 remains in the supported-target matrix, but is never binary-distributed
build_from_source_assessment.documented_approach: cross-compilation from x86_64 with an arm-linux-gnueabihf toolchain; QEMU route is documented as ARM64-only
build_from_source_assessment.native_build_on_device: NOT VIABLE. Official docs state the build needs more than 2GB memory and that a 32-bit compiler may lack memory to run the build. Target has ~483 MiB available and no swap.
build_from_source_assessment.toolchain_gap: target cmake 3.18.4 satisfies only onnxruntime <= ~1.12 (cmake_minimum_required 3.18); 1.16+ requires cmake >= 3.26

unofficial_candidates_not_verified.relevance: publishes bullseye cp39 linux_armv7l wheels up to 1.16.0
unofficial_candidates_not_verified.status: UNOFFICIAL, no warranty, not smoke-tested on Norns, no redistribution assessment performed

unofficial_candidates_not_verified.relevance: 1.17.3 C/C++ shared library only, armv7-a NEON hard-float
unofficial_candidates_not_verified.status: UNOFFICIAL, no Python wheel, not smoke-tested on Norns

alternative_runtimes_surveyed.name: tract (sonos, Rust)
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.armv7: first-class: CI builds armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf; hand-written ARMv7 NEON kernels
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.python39: ctypes binding over a cross-built cdylib; no PyPI armv7 wheel
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.note: strongest candidate on paper; unverified on device

alternative_runtimes_surveyed.name: ncnn
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.armv7: prebuilt manylinux_2_31_armv7l cp39 wheels on PyPI

alternative_runtimes_surveyed.name: tflite-runtime
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.note: successor ai-edge-litert publishes no armv7l wheels

alternative_runtimes_surveyed.name: ggml/llama.cpp/whisper.cpp
alternative_runtimes_surveyed.armv7: 32-bit builds broken; upstream issue closed as not planned

unresolved: None of the unofficial or alternative runtimes has been smoke-tested on the actual Norns device.
Whether Norns ships numpy, and its exact glibc version, remain unchecked on device.
No Microsoft announcement formally dropping ARM32 was found; the absence appears to be 'never released' rather than 'dropped on a date'.
UMXHQ currently runs under PyTorch, which remains an uncredible Norns deployment dependency regardless of this finding.
consequence: Any Norns deployment of the pinned pretrained chain requires either a cross-compiled ONNX Runtime armv7l build produced off-device, or a different runtime such as tract. No official-wheel path exists. This does not by itself invalidate the desktop quality measurement.
